title: Peripherals: monitor, keyboard, mouse, printer and scanner

videos.script: The first two lessons were inside the box. This one is everything you actually touch. {{touch}} A peripheral is a translator. A keyboard turns a finger into a character, a mouse turns a movement into coordinates, a scanner turns paper into pixels, and a monitor and a printer run the same machinery backwards. {{translate}} That framing matters because it says where the failures are. Nothing here computes anything, so nothing here is slow the way a hard disk is slow. What goes wrong instead is a translation that is wrong or expensive: a resolution the screen cannot really show, a keyboard that cannot type your own language without a fight, a printer whose ink costs more than the printer did. {{fail}} Two of those are paid for twice, and the last one is the largest single waste of money anywhere in this course. {{money}} We finish on the two pictures you will be asked to put names on, because the regions of a keyboard and the inside of a scanner are both things you have looked at for years without ever being told what they are called.
